scope: Original Anima (a1) control with a reference image and a prompt that matches it
question: The first round paired a standing-bicycle prompt with a seated reference and produced degraded limbs. This round separates a control fault from a prompt/reference mismatch by keeping the reference and changing only how the prompt describes it.

isolated_runtime.source: snapshot/runtime with the deployed a1 workflows
isolated_runtime.models: referenced from the live model directories, never copied

fixed_parameters.reference_note: The line-art character sketch supplied in a previous erasing round; it holds the pose and composition the control branch must transfer.
fixed_parameters.advanced_erase_subgraph: removed for the control cases so the full control map reaches the apply node

prompts.matched: anime illustration, anime girl, long dark hair, hair bow, ruffled dress, leaning forward with one arm reaching up, face turned downward and away, seen from the side, close upper body framing, soft indoor lighting, masterpiece, very aesthetic, high quality, detailed
prompts.mismatched: A full body illustration of an adult woman wearing a blue raincoat, dark trousers and yellow boots, standing beside a red bicycle on a quiet city street, soft overcast daylight, clear composition, detailed face and hands.
prompts.appearance: same pose and framing as matched, with blonde hair, blue eyes and a white short dress instead of the dark-haired ruffled-dress description

cases.erase: advanced subgraph left active with the saved mask

mismatched_vs_matched.reading: One reference image and one sampler seed; only the prompt's description of the subject changed, and the render changes completely. The prompt, not the control, decides whether the limbs read as intact.

appearance_vs_matched.reading: Same pose and framing, different hair, eye colour and outfit: the control holds the pose while the prompt still controls appearance.

strength_check.reason: A first pair of runs at this seed produced byte-equal pixels at strength 1 and 0.63, so the strength path was re-probed instead of being reported as a no-op.
strength_check.probe: the same graph submitted at strengths 1.0, 0.8, 0.63 and 0.4 with one fixed seed

strength_zero.reading: strength 0.0 differs from strength 1.0 by mean absolute difference 36.8-38.9, so the control path is active

strength_check.conclusion: strength reaches sampling; the earlier equal pair was not reproducible

erase_mask_behaviour.live_mask: the saved erase mask in the run input directory is fully opaque, and LoadImage exposes a single-channel image as 1 - alpha, so the composite is a no-op
erase_mask_behaviour.evidence: the erase case and an equivalent case with the whole advanced subgraph removed render byte-identical pixels
erase_mask_behaviour.earlier_round: a transparent-rectangle mask did change the control image inside the mask region, so erasing itself works; the recorded mask is simply not transparent
erase_mask_behaviour.effect_on_quality: not the cause of the degraded limbs; with a no-op composite the control map is already the preprocessor output

limits: One reference, one seed and one neutral prompt family; not a general quality certification.
Soft or unresolved areas remain where the line-art reference carries little structure; this round does not claim an artifact-free render at strength 1.
Two-image control (pose reference plus a separate colour reference) is not expressible without adding a model or node to the deployed workflow, so it was not tested.
The line-art reference supplied by the user is exposed artwork and is used only inside the isolated runtime; the deployment scope is unchanged.
